text: Abdul Waheed Khan, born in 1947 in Agya (Sant kabir Nagar), India, earned a master's degree in agricultural extension from Agra University in 1965. He then moved to the University of Wisconsin in Madison, Wisconsin, where he obtained a master's degree in agricultural journalism in 1970 and a Doctor of Philosophy in mass communication in 1973. Prior to joining the United Nations, Khan served as Founding Director and Professor of the Communications Division at the Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU) in New Delhi, India, until 1992. During his final year at IGNOU, he also served as a visiting professor at the National Institute of Multimedia Education in Chiba, Japan. In 1992, he began working at the Commonwealth of Learning in Canada as a Senior Programme Officer. From 1995 to 1998, he served as Acting Head of the Communications and Information Technologies Division before becoming Principal Communications Specialist, a role he held until 1998. In 1998, he returned to IGNOU as President and Chief Executive Officer (Vice-Chancellor), a position he held until 2000. During that period, he spent a year as Director of Training and Development at the Commonwealth of Learning. In 2001, he was appointed Assistant Director-General for Communication and Information at the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), a role he held from 2001 to 2010. He was President of a start-up business university in Manama, Bahrain until March 2013. Currently retired, Khan spends his time between India and Canada, where he settled after leaving Bahrain. He is a member of the Council of Presidents for the University of the People, an organization that established the first non-profit, tuition-free, online academic institution aimed at revolutionizing higher education by providing college-level studies to students worldwide.
